BIRTHDAY WEBSITE IDEAS · WISHLY GUIDE

How to Make a Free Birthday Website: A Practical No-Code Guide

Learn how to create a personal birthday website for free with a ready-made template, photos, a heartfelt message and one shareable link.

A birthday website can bring a greeting, favourite photos and a personal message together in one link. You do not need to build a site from a blank page or learn web development first. This guide explains how to plan a simple birthday page, create it with a free-to-start template, check the visitor experience and share it responsibly.

Birthday Website Ideas9 min readUpdated 17 November 2026

Decide what the birthday page should do

Choose one clear purpose

Start with the feeling you want the person to take away. A page for a partner might tell a shared story; a page for a parent may collect family memories; a page for a friend can be playful and full of inside jokes. A clear purpose helps you choose the right template and avoid filling the page with unrelated effects.

Make a short content list

Before opening the editor, gather the recipient’s name, the birthday date, three to six suitable photos and the message you want them to read. If the design supports music or video, choose media you have permission to use and that the recipient will enjoy.

Choose a free-to-start birthday website template

Compare the preview, not only the thumbnail

Open a few birthday designs and look at the actual preview. Check whether the layout has room for your message, whether its photo areas suit portrait or landscape images and whether the interactions match the recipient’s personality. Wishly’s official site describes a free-to-start workflow with ready-made templates; check the current editor and plan details before relying on a particular option.

Understand what “free” means

A free-to-start service lets you begin creating without paying at the first step, but individual services can still have limits or optional paid features. Review the current plan, storage, publishing and template terms shown in your account. Do not assume every template, upload size or feature is unlimited.

Personalise the page with meaningful details

Replace every sample field

Change the sample name, greeting, captions, dates and any placeholder text. A single incorrect sample name can make a thoughtful page feel unfinished. Use a natural voice rather than copying a long generic birthday paragraph.

Choose photos that tell a small story

Use a few clear images instead of uploading everything. A first photo can introduce the person, the next can show a shared memory and the last can look ahead to another year. Check image crops and make sure everyone shown would be comfortable with the photo being shared.

Use design choices to support readability

A colour palette and font should make the page feel consistent while keeping the message easy to read on a phone. If the chosen template offers audio, video, reveals or other interactions, test each one and keep only what adds value.

Preview the page before publishing

Read it as the recipient

Switch to Preview and go through the page from the opening screen to the final section. Check spelling, names, pronouns, dates, photo crops, buttons and any template-specific interaction. Ask a trusted person to review sensitive or public-facing wording if appropriate.

Test it on a phone

Open the preview on a small screen. Make sure text is readable, buttons are easy to tap and images load correctly. A page that looks good on a desktop can still feel crowded on mobile.

Publish and share the birthday website

Use one clear share message

After publishing, open the public link in a separate browser to confirm the visitor-facing version. Send it with a short message such as, “I made a little birthday page for you—open it when you have a quiet minute.” The recipient should not need to install a special app if the page is published as a normal web link.

Choose the right privacy level

A shareable link is not automatically private. Avoid including phone numbers, home addresses, private conversations or photos that the recipient has not agreed to share. If the selected Wishly template or feature offers password protection, use it only after checking how it works and share the password through a separate channel.

A simple birthday website checklist

Before you send the link

Confirm the recipient’s name and birthday; remove demo content; check that every image is appropriate; test the mobile view; confirm the live link; and make sure the page says what you intended. Keep a copy of the message and source photos in case you want to update the page later.

Frequently asked questions

Can I make a birthday website for free?

Wishly describes itself as free to start, so you can begin with an account and a template without an upfront creation fee. Check the current account limits and any optional paid features before publishing.

Do I need coding or hosting?

No coding is needed to use a ready-made Wishly template. The official site says Wishly hosts published pages, so you do not need to buy a separate domain or hosting plan for a normal Wishly page.

Can I make the page from my phone?

Yes. Wishly says its builder is designed for phone and desktop use. Preview the finished page on the same kind of screen your recipient is likely to use.

Can I edit the page after sharing it?

Wishly’s official FAQ says you can return to the dashboard, edit the page and publish again while keeping the same link. Always reopen the live link after updating it.

Wishly features and editor options may change. Check the selected template preview and current interface for the latest available controls.
